metadata.research_goal: Deepen boxing footwork, ringcraft, range control, ring-zone, exit, and open-stance foot-position knowledge for app-facing teaching and retrieval.

key_concepts.summary: Footwork is only good if stance, guard, balance, punch readiness, and defense readiness survive movement.
Ringcraft depends on repeated small adjustments, not large jumps.
Center, ropes, and corners change available exits, contact risk, and tactical priorities.
Pressure fighters should cut lanes, not chase the opponent's body.
Jab range, mid range, inside range, and clinch/reset range require different punch and defense choices.
Orthodox/southpaw foot battles should be introduced after basic stance and step-slide control.

technical_models.model: Balanced 45-degree stance, shoulder-width base, soft knees, light rear heel, chin protected, hands available.
Foot nearest the direction moves first; second foot slides back to stance.
Plant lead or rear foot, rotate body, move free foot to create a new 30-90 degree angle.
Hold center, match circle, take exit side, force backward, trap ropes/corner, attack without smothering.

tactical_rules.rule: Increase speed only while stance width, guard, and balance stay stable.
Use short steps for control before adding bounce, rhythm changes, or angles.
Pressure should take away exits; following lets the opponent keep circling.
Beginners should learn center-ring movement before rope or corner tactics.
Rope work needs defined exit skill and contact constraints.
Jab range favors straight punches and exits; inside range requires tighter punches and faster resets.
Teach lead-foot awareness and rear-hand lane before advanced southpaw traps.
Late-round footwork should bias step-slide, jab, pivot, and clinch/reset over complex angle chains.

physical_demands.quality: Calf, Achilles, foot intrinsic, and ankle stiffness for repeated direction changes.
Hip abductor/adductor and glute control for lateral movement and pivots.
Trunk stiffness plus hip rotation for angle changes without losing punch mechanics.
Aerobic recovery to preserve ring control across rounds.
Visual tracking and ring awareness for ropes, corners, stance, and scoring.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Jump-rope spikes, bouncing, hard floors, or large footwork volume jumps can irritate ankle/calf/Achilles.
Planted foot without hip turn can increase knee torque during pivots.
Orthodox/southpaw lead-foot battles can create foot clashes and balance disruptions.
Poor exits and corner trap sparring can raise contact risk.
Repeated pivots with stuck feet can increase low-back or hip irritation.

training_implications.summary: Beginner assessment: move 60-90 seconds without crossing feet, hopping, squaring up, or losing guard.
Intermediate work should add pivot exits, angles after jab/cross, lane cutting, and basic open-stance awareness.
Advanced work should include opponent-specific ringcraft, pressure vs mover, feint steering, rope tactics, and score-state control.
Track footwork minutes, jump-rope minutes, pivot reps, surface, and ankle/knee pain flags.
Use ring zone and range tags in retrieval for technical/tactical workout generation.
